newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWA eyes bid for NSW TAB - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWA eyes bid for NSW TAB - paper.

text.p: Electronics group AWA Ltd is looking at bidding up to A$750 million to buy 75 percent of the New South Wales government-owned betting agency the Totalisator Agency Board (TAB), The Sydney Morning Herald reported on Wednesday.

"AWA is looking to raise the cash to pay for the TAB by issuing new shares. If its bid was acceptable to the state government, a combined AWA and NSW TAB would become a listed company," the newspaper said.
AWA's largest shareholder, Reg Grundy's RG Capital, supported the idea in principle, the Herald said.
The New South Wales government had not yet approved the privatisation of the TAB, but would address the issue in the next few weeks, the newspaper said.
"If the government gives the go-ahead, TAB will be put up for tender, with a sharemarket float said to be the preferred option," the Herald said.

"It is understood the government has received advice that a trade sale of the TAB would be a simpler process and receive a higher price. AWA's proposal would provide the government with a trade sale, but still allow the public to invest in the TAB on the sharemarket."
